author: fradamt
content:
Trying to break down the problems, I think there's two:
1) what to do with validators that are not registered. 
2) what to do about pre-fork attestations, which may conflict with each other or with post-fork PQ attestations

For 1), we could only fork once we have >= 100 - X stake registered, for X sufficiently higher than 1/3, i.e. set a threshold like 80% or 90% or something. Then, exiting the at most X remaining stake all at once gives a safety loss of at most 2/3 X. For example, with X = 10 we'd fork once we hit 90% registration, and the safety loss would be ~6.6%, so the baseline guarantee would start from ~26% slashing instead of 1/3. This is safety loss purely from reducing the validator set and thus the quorum intersection.

Note that even with a long withdrawal delay and willingness to socially slash, the safety hit is there, like Terence said somewhere above: we're anyway changing the composition of the validator set very fast, reducing the quorum by 2/3 X (or 2/3 of whatever the exiting stake is) and thus reducing quorum intersection by that much. In the case of an attack that exploits this to get conflicting finality cross-fork with reduced slashing (reduced quorum intersection), it's not the exiting validators that would double sign, since they don't exist on the post-fork chain. The only alternative to this would be not reduce the quorum, which essentially looks like treating the non-PQ validators as active even if they cannot participate. That's just a safety liveness tradeoff: at the extreme X = 1/3 (we fork as soon as we have 2/3) but we still require a 2/3 quorum, so that we cannot tolerate any amount of non-participating stake among the PQ keys.

author: fradamt
content: For 2), either automatic or manual processing of BLS-BLS slashings and BLS-PQ slashings after the fork is required. We don't necessarily need a long withdrawal delay for the non-PQ validators that exit at the fork, we could just accept the safety hit from those, which would be at most X (all of the X non-PQ stake double signs pre-fork, while they're still active), so only X/3 more than the unavoidable safety hit discussed above. Concretely, with X = 10% we'd go from 26% to 23% if we didn't have a long withdrawal delay and just let them all withdraw quickly. The bigger issue is everyone else (the 100 - X PQ validators), but it's still not much of an issue because they continue being active after the fork and there's plenty of time to figure out how to punish them if double finality were to happen in a way that actually causes problems

author: fradamt
content: In conclusion, I don't think the special withdrawal delay is particularly needed, though it's quite cheap to implement. More importantly, I don't think big preparations for social slashing are really necessary. For the non-PQ validators, it barely makes a difference, and the real defense is just to only fork once we have a sufficiently low amount of non-PQ stake. For the PQ validators, there's not much time pressure since they are subject to normal exit queues

author: m.kalinin
content:
> and the safety loss would be ~6.6%

I think the way to look at this is that there is an immediate safety decay of 6.6% or whatever else this number is. With Gloas we have 10% safety decay for a week of WS period with the total amount of stake at today's level. Given that we will have 16.6% in total it roughly shrinks down the WS period by two times.

author: m.kalinin
content:
> BLS-PQ slashings after the fork is required

This is to handle surround votes, right? Won't be possible to be processed onchain unless we keep BLS pubkeys after the fork

author: fradamt
content: Yes. Also won't be able to process BLS-BLS ones after the fork (e.g. conflicting finality happens just before the fork) in that case. But I think that's fine, that's why I said "or manual processing".

author: m.kalinin
content: After the network finalizes for the first time post-fork, I think conflicting finality before the fork boundary shouldn't be that much of a problem. It's just that the checkpoint-sync must be required to be run with a post-fork checkpoint which doesn't sound like an unreasonable counter-measure around that fork

author: m.kalinin
content: Which seem to make manual slashing a good enough way to handle cross-fork equivocations as very likely it won't be needed

author: fradamt
content: yes as soon as we finalize post-fork we're fine

author: fradamt
content: it's just that in principle we cannot know that we will

author: fradamt
content: (but again, I am very much in favor of keeping this simple and not overdoing response to theoretical concerns)
